title: Value of Faith Over Worldly Gains
summary: This hadith emphasizes that faith is the most important blessing from Allah. Without faith, one cannot enter paradise and will face eternal displeasure in hell. Material wealth and worldly comforts mean nothing without faith. Conversely, a poor person who believes in Allah and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) will eventually be rewarded with paradise. The Quran warns against abandoning one’s faith, as it leads to the nullification of good deeds and results in hell as the final abode. Therefore, valuing and adhering to faith is paramount.
translation: Of all the blessings that Allah has given us, faith is the greatest and most important. It is solely through faith that we can enter paradise. Without faith, one faces an eternal existence in a place called hell, which is extremely dangerous and painful. Hence, even if a person lives a prosperous life with health, joy, and all sorts of conveniences—like fine clothes, a nice car, a good house, and excellent staff—if they do not end their life with faith, they will end up in a place everyone should seek refuge from, known as hell. Conversely, if someone is homeless or poorly dressed, without even basic food, but believes in worshiping Allah, the Essence of Allah, and the Prophethood of the Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him), despite any sins, they will ultimately be rewarded with paradise. This paradise is such a magnificent palace, a splendid garden, and a marvelous place that no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no mind has imagined. Therefore, one should remember to value the blessing of faith given by Allah. When something is not valued, it is taken away. Hence, express gratitude to Allah for being a person of faith and strictly follow His commands. The Quran states, 'And whoever among you turns back from their religion and dies as a disbeliever, their deeds will be of no avail in this world and the Hereafter.' Hence, those who turn away from their religion, do not value their faith, or deny the foundational and subsidiary aspects of their religion, either practically or in belief, will have their good deeds nullified, and hell will be their ultimate abode. Therefore, it should always be remembered that faith is a significant blessing among all blessings of Allah, and it should be valued, adhering strictly to its obligatory acts. Pray to Allah and ask Him to keep us steadfast on this path of guidance until the very end.
